scams.name: The Fukutomicho Drug-and-Charge Blackout Scam
scams.description: Hustlers near Kannai or Isezakicho approach tourists offering cheap girls bars. Victims follow them into snack bars in Fukutomicho where they consume drinks potentially spiked with substances, lose consciousness, and wake with unauthorized charges exceeding ¥600,000. Police documented 249 victims losing ¥147.39 million in 11 months of 2023, with one victim charged ¥2.7 million in a single night.
scams.avoidance: Treat Fukutomicho as a no-go zone after dark. Never follow hustlers (now illegal under May 2025 ordinance). Refuse drinks you didn't watch poured. Stay on main Noge streets with open-front venues. Set low ATM withdrawal limits and card transaction caps before traveling. Contact Isezaki Police Station if blackout and unauthorized charges occur.

scams.name: The Chinatown All-You-Can-Eat 6-Order Limit & Leftover Surcharge
scams.description: Chinatown all-you-can-eat restaurants advertise unlimited dining at ¥2,500 for 90 minutes but enforce hidden rules: only 6 items ordered at once, with leftovers triggering surcharges up to ¥15,000 never displayed on street signage or menus. Rules are announced only after customers sit down.
scams.avoidance: Only eat at shops with Yokohama Chinatown Development Association certification plaques. Stick to venues rated 4.3+ with 500+ Japanese reviews. Avoid plainclothes hustlers soliciting outside. Ask explicitly about order limits and leftover surcharges in writing before sitting. Photograph menus and posted rules. Prefer family-style or shops advertising 食べ残し無料 (no leftover surcharge).

scams.name: The Yokohama Station West Exit Hustler-Izakaya Trap
scams.description: Hustlers with clipboards near Yokohama Station West Exit approach tourists with offers of ¥1,300 all-you-can-drink specials. After collecting ¥500-1,000 upfront 'deposits,' venues add undisclosed mandatory minimums, service charges, and premium otoshi fees that double the advertised price.
scams.avoidance: Pre-book venues on Tabelog or Google Maps before leaving your hotel. Exit via East Exit or Minatomirai walkway to avoid hustler concentration. Never hand cash deposits to hustlers. Ask explicitly about otoshi, service charges, and minimum-order rules before sitting. Call 110 and cite the Kanagawa Nuisance Prevention Ordinance if pressured.
scams.location: Yokohama Station West Exit, Minami-Saiwai-bashi, Nishi-ku (near Bibre and Don Quijote)

scams.name: The Noge Girls Bar / Komachi-dori Hostess Overcharge
scams.description: Girls bars on and around Komachi-dori in Noge employ street solicitation tactics to lure customers into dimly-lit upstairs venues. Hostess charges are never quoted upfront, and bills often exceed ¥100,000 for 90 minutes without itemization.
scams.avoidance: Stick to Noge izakaya with 4.5+ Google ratings and 500+ reviews. Only enter bars with printed menus visible from the street. Check the Noge Tourism Association map (noge-kankou.org) which flags problem venues. Refuse any hostess joining your table unless per-hour charges are printed. Request itemized written bills before paying. Call 110 under post-May-2025 ordinance if pressured.
scams.location: Noge yokocho, Komachi-dori, Sakuragicho side, Naka-ku; Isezaki-cho Fukutomi-cho adjacent

scams.name: The Chinatown Sweet Chestnut Sample-Then-Force-Sell
scams.description: Vendors on Chinatown's main street offer free samples of amaguri (sweet chestnuts) to passersby. Once a sample is accepted, vendors immediately begin bagging a full kilogram and pressure customers to purchase at inflated prices. Refusing feels socially difficult, which is the deliberate design.
scams.avoidance: Do not accept the sample—refusal after accepting feels socially impossible by design. Only buy from stalls displaying Yokohama Chinatown Development Association certification. Confirm per-bag prices aloud in Japanese before vendors bag anything. Report overcharges to Yokohama City Consumer Affairs Center or Kagacho Police with photos. Prefer packaged chestnuts from established confectioneries.
scams.location: Yokohama Chinatown main street (中華街大通り) and side alleys, Naka-ku

scams.name: The Yokohama Station / Haneda Airport Taxi Meter Games
scams.description: Taxi drivers at Yokohama Station West Exit quote discounts then add mystery surcharges pushing fares ¥2,000 over standard meter rates. At Haneda Airport, independent operators repeatedly toggle highway-mode during rides, inflating ¥7,000 trips to ¥8,000+.
scams.avoidance: Use only official licensed taxi queues with green license plates. Pre-check expected fares on NAVITIME or GO app before boarding. Request itemized receipts (領収書) by law. Use GO or Uber apps for upfront fare computation. For Haneda-to-Yokohama, take Keikyu Airport Line (¥500) or Limousine Bus (¥650) instead. Report overcharges with plate photos to Kanagawa Transport Bureau or 110.
scams.location: Yokohama Station West Exit taxi rank; Haneda Airport arrivals to Yokohama
